overview: The Duty Drawback Scheme is a customs duty refund mechanism under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) that reimburses exporters for duties paid on imported inputs used in the manufacture of export goods. It aims to enhance the competitiveness of Indian exports by neutralizing the incidence of taxes and duties on inputs used in export production. The scheme operates under the Customs Act, 1962 and is administered by CBIC to promote export-oriented industrialization and reduce the cost burden on exporters.
objectives: To refund customs and central excise duties paid on inputs used in the manufacture of export goods
To neutralize the incidence of taxes and duties on inputs used for export production
To enhance the international competitiveness of Indian exports
To promote export-oriented industrialization and value addition in domestic manufacturing
To reduce the cost burden on exporters and improve realization in global markets
eligibility: Exporters who have paid customs duty on imported inputs or central excise duty on indigenous inputs used in the manufacture of goods that are subsequently exported are eligible for duty drawback. The claim must be filed within the prescribed time limit from the date of export, and the exporter must maintain proper records of import, usage in production, and export.
benefits: Financial reimbursement of customs and central excise duties paid on inputs used in export production; neutralization of tax burden on exports; improved price competitiveness in international markets; encouragement of value addition and import substitution in export-oriented sectors; compliance with WTO principles by not constituting a subsidy but a tax remission.
financial_support: The scheme provides refund of customs duty paid on imported inputs and central excise duty paid on indigenous inputs used in the manufacture of export goods. The drawback rate is fixed as a percentage of the FOB value of exports or as a fixed amount per unit, based on the input-output norms notified by CBIC. Refunds are credited directly to the exporter's bank account via electronic transfer after verification of shipping bills and other documentation.
application_process: 1. Determine eligibility based on import of inputs and subsequent export of finished goods. 2. Maintain records of bills of entry, warehouse documents, production records, and shipping bills. 3. File drawback claim electronically through the ICEGATE portal along with shipping bill and proof of export. 4. Submit supporting documents such as bills of entry, bank realization certificate, and consent letter if applicable. 5. Claim is processed by the jurisdictional Customs Office after verification of documents and adherence to time limits. 6. Upon approval, drawback amount is credited to the exporter's bank account.
required_documents: Bill of Entry for imported inputs
Bank Realization Certificate (BRC) or Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC)
Proof of payment of customs duty
Consent letter from the manufacturer (if exporter is not the manufacturer)
Declaration regarding non-availment of CENVAT credit or other exemptions
Bank account details for refund credit
deadlines: Claims must be filed within 12 months from the date of let export of the goods, as per Section 75 of the Customs Act, 1962.
implementing_agency: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
caveats: Drawback is not available if CENVAT credit or input tax credit under GST has been availed on the same inputs
Claims are time-barred if not filed within 12 months from the date of export
Drawback rates are subject to periodic revision based on input-output norms
Refund may be withheld or rejected if documents are incomplete or discrepancies are found
No drawback is allowed on goods exported under bond or letter of undertaking (LUT) without payment of IGST
